title: Prove nine calls are necessary for three abelian bit registers
body:
The pinned version of #288 leaves the abelian three-register bit cases with seven or eight calls open. This proves that **nine calls are necessary and sufficient** when paid frames are nonzero rational rank-one matrices and all three target frames are invertible and lower triangular.

The proof reduces the remaining span-five case to 2,276 scalar families and checks all 21,317,520 orders. Two separate exact engines agree on every family: 415,398 diagonal terminals, zero survivors. The argument covers unbounded rational frame coefficients; it is not a bounded coefficient search.

The seven-file package contains the proof, catalogue generator, two engines, controls, and a replay command. It requires Python and a C++17 compiler and includes no generated search data. Attribution and AI assistance are stated in the proof.

Validation: `python3 research/bit-three-register-lower-bound/replay.py` passes. The result does not change κ and does not cover extra registers or arbitrary free address maps between paid calls.

The existing `gen4-bank-verify` target also passes. `make verify` stops at the existing `joint-dual-verify` source-hash assertion for `Makefile`; the same failure was reproduced on unchanged base `12a4934`. This PR does not change the affected files. The remaining `verify-pair` and `verify-tests` groups pass when run separately.
